sections.title: Cap
sections.text: The cap is usually 4–10 cm wide, hemispherical or convex at first and later more expanded. Its smooth surface becomes viscid when damp; the centre is often ochre to brownish, with a paler cream to whitish margin.

sections.title: Gills, stem and smell
sections.text: The crowded gills start pale and become clay-brown to dull brown. Their pale edge can bear tiny droplets in damp weather; these may dry into brown spots. The whitish, floccose or pruinose stem is often 4–7 cm tall (larger specimens occur) and has no ring. The flesh is white and has a characteristic radish smell; the taste is sometimes bitter.

sections.title: Habitat and identification
sections.text: This ectomycorrhizal fungus grows on soil near trees, including in broadleaf woods, parks, avenues and roadsides; it may also associate with conifers. Fruiting is mainly in late summer and autumn, with regional variation. Several close species share these features: identification to species level may require microscopic examination of spores and cystidia; a photograph alone is not enough.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: Hebeloma crustuliniforme is reported as poisonous and can cause gastrointestinal upset. Toxicity lists also classify the genus Hebeloma among gastrointestinal-syndrome mushrooms. Do not eat a specimen identified from an image; after a suspected ingestion, contact a poison centre or emergency services.

traits: Cap 4–10 cm wide, convex then expanded, smooth and viscid when damp; ochre to brownish centre with a pale margin
Crowded gills, pale at first then clay-brown to dull brown, with a pale edge
Tiny droplets often visible along the edges of damp gills; brown spots may remain when they dry
Whitish, floccose or pruinose stem, usually without a ring
White flesh, radish smell, sometimes bitter taste; brownish to olive-brown spore print
On soil near trees, including woods, parks, avenues and roadsides; mainly late summer and autumn
Poisonous; the H. crustuliniforme group includes close species that are difficult to separate without microscopy
safetyNote: Poisonous: gastrointestinal upset is possible. Several Hebeloma look alike and may require microscopy to separate; do not eat a mushroom identified from a photo. After a suspected ingestion, contact a poison centre or emergency services.
